answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut, the incumbent has refused to reopen price (limiting negotiate_terms per memory_c4's prior success but blocked now), and the contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew — so renew or defer risks a supply gap on a line running at 94% with no buffer. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate alone, and memory_c2 records a prior quick, accurate onboarding with this vendor. However, switching the full primary volume at once would concentrate delivery risk exactly when there is no buffer, so the intent is a guarded switch: transition primary supply to the low-cost vendor with staged volume ramp and expedited qualification, keeping the incumbent on short interim terms as fallback if possible. Memory_c2 is verified before committing because the entire cost case rests on that vendor relationship being as reliable as the consolidated memory claims; memory_c3's dual-sourcing lesson informs keeping a fallback path rather than a clean cutover.
